# Template: binscatter
A binned scatter plot: the workhorse figure for showing a relationship between two variables — raw data averaged into equal-sized bins so the shape emerges, with a fitted curve through them. Relationship shapes: rising, falling, concave, convex, U-shaped, or none. Choose this scene for ANY request about a binned scatter or binscatter, the correlation or relationship between two variables, a scatter plot with a fitted or regression line, or income/education/health gradient figures.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "relationship": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "linear_up",
    "linear_down",
    "concave",
    "convex",
    "u_shape",
    "none"
   ],
   "description": "Shape of the underlying relationship (default linear_up)."
  },
  "noise": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Vertical scatter of the bin dots, 0-1 (default 0.35)."
  },
  "show_fit": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Fitted curve through the bins (default true)."
  },
  "x_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Default \"X\"."
  },
  "y_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Default \"Y\"."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the coordinate axes (a group with captions)
- dots: the binned dots (a group)
- fit: the fitted curve (when show_fit)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw a binned scatter showing a positive relationship." → params: {"x_label":"Years of schooling","y_label":"Log earnings","title":"The education gradient"}
Request: "Show a U-shaped binscatter." → params: {"relationship":"u_shape","title":"A U-shaped relationship"}

In YAML: `template: binscatter` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
